MUQATIL:23:112-116/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:112-116/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:112-116/r1.claim: God asks how many years the unbelievers stayed in the world, meaning their graves.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p419#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p419#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p419#2/r1.claim: God asks the dead in the Hereafter how many years they remained on earth to make them see how little their worldly stay was.

FARRA:v2p243/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p243/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p243/r5.claim: Medina reads قال كم لبثتم, while Kufa reads قل كم لبثتم.

TAB-FULL:v17p129/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p129/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p129/r1.claim: Most Medinan, Basran, and some Kufan readers take “he said” as a report: God asks the people of Hell how long they stayed, and they say a day or part of one because punishment makes worldly time seem short.

TAB-FULL:v17p129/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p129/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p129/r2.claim: Most Kufan readers instead read an imperative, “say,” reflecting their codex spelling without the alif; other codices have the alif.

TAB-FULL:v17p129/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p129/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p129/r3.claim: The declarative reading is preferable: the surrounding address is plural, so a command would naturally be plural “say”; singular “say” is possible, but declarative singular is more fluent Arabic.

ZAJJAJ:v4p24#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p24#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p24#2/r2.claim: كم is accusative with لبثتم; عدد سنين is governed by كم, and doubled tāʾ is permitted in question and answer.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r5.speaker: ابن كثير في رواية البزي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r5.claim: Al-Bazzī transmits Ibn Kathīr's imperative قل كم لبثتم and indicative قل إن لبثتم, without assimilating the thāʾ in لبثتم.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r6.speaker: قنبل عن النبال عن أصحابه عن ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r6.claim: Qunbul's transmission has قل in both positions without alif.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r7.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r7.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī use the imperative in both positions and assimilate the thāʾ in لبثتم.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r8.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p448/r8.claim: These readers use the alif form in both positions as indicative statements.

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2511/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2511/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2511/r1.claim: A report says God asks the people of Paradise how long they lived on earth; they answer a day or part of one, and God calls it a good trade for his mercy, approval, and Paradise. He asks the people of Hell likewise and calls their earthly life a bad trade for his wrath and fire.

NAHHAS:v3p123/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p123/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p123/r7.claim: The two questions ‘how long did you remain?’ have different senses and neither is better; ʿadada sinīn has a sound masculine plural accusative, though some Arabs use a genitive with tanwīn.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r1.claim: Al-Bazzī's transmission from Ibn Kathīr has an imperative at the question and a reported statement at the answer; Qunbul's cited transmission has imperatives at both places.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r2.speaker: نافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r2.claim: These readers use قال at both locations, presenting both clauses as reports rather than commands.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r3.claim: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read قل at both locations, addressing the questioner with an imperative; the Kufan codex reading قل supports their choice.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p306#3/r4.claim: These readers assimilate thāʾ into tāʾ because their articulation points are close and both are voiceless; Ibn Kathīr favors clear separation because the articulation points differ.

THALABI:v7p59/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p59/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p59/r1.claim: They forget how long they lived in the world because of the great torment; the question rebukes deniers of resurrection and establishes the argument against them.

THALABI:v7p59/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p59/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
THALABI:v7p59/r2.claim: They read قل كم as a command, matching Kufan codices without alif; it can address the group or each unbeliever individually.

THALABI:v7p59/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p59/r3.speaker: باقي القراء
THALABI:v7p59/r3.claim: They read قال in both places, matching their codices with alif and making God the speaker.

THALABI:v7p59/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p59/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
THALABI:v7p59/r4.claim: He reads قل كم first as a command, then قال as the reported answer, which the author calls an evident reading.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p68#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p68#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p68#2/r1.claim: They may be asked how long they lived in the world, which seems slight beside punishment in Hell.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p68#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p68#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p68#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, they are asked about their graves; the brief answer reports what they knew, not a lie.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p68#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p68#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p68#2/r3.claim: The people asked to count time are angels.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p68#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p68#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p68#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, they are calculators or those who reckon time.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p82/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p82/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p82/r1.claim: God asks the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection how many years they remained in the earth, meaning in their graves, as a rebuke for denying resurrection.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p82/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p82/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p82/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses كم as accusative governed by لبثتم, while عدد سنين is accusative as its specification.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p82/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p82/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p82/r3.claim: A reading with قل can address the disbeliever being questioned about how long he remained.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p82/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p82/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p82/r4.claim: Alternatively, قل is an instruction to the person who questions them on the Day of Resurrection about their stay.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:110-113/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:110-113/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:110-113/r3.claim: After raising deniers of resurrection from their graves, God asks how many years they remained there as a rebuke.

JISHUMI:v7p5098/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5098/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
JISHUMI:v7p5098/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir reads قل كم لبثتم as a command and قال إن لبثتم as a statement, which suits the second as an answer.

JISHUMI:v7p5098/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5098/r5.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي
JISHUMI:v7p5098/r5.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read both verbs as commands, matching Kufa codices; other codices and readers use indicative forms, with قل addressed to the singular Prophet as a collective command.

JISHUMI:v7p5098/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5098/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5098/r6.claim: Sukhr is mockery; nisyān means the opposite of remembering and also leaving something, with the latter closer to its sense here; labth and mukth mean remaining over time.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p432/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p432/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p432/r1.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read قل as an imperative addressing the group or each disbeliever; others read قال in both places. Ibn Kathīr also reads the imperative.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p208#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p208#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p208#2/r1.claim: Kufan codices have “He said,” while the codices of the two sanctuaries, Basra and Syria have “Say.”

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p208#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p208#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p208#2/r2.claim: With “He said,” the speaker may be God or an angel commanded to question them; in “He said, how long…,” the speaker may be the angel or a chief of Hell’s inhabitants.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r1.speaker: نافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r1.claim: These readers have qala kam labithtum and qul in labithtum; other readers vary between a command or report for the first verb.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r2.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi use qul for both questions and statements, while al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir has a command for the question and a report for the answer.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r3.claim: The readings mean either God asks and then tells them the stay was brief, an individual is ordered to answer and corrected, or they are questioned before being told the answer.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r4.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r4.claim: Al-Tabari understands their stay in the earth as their living time in this world; they have forgotten through torment and estimate only a day or part of one.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the time they lay dead in the earth, since they denied resurrection and are now asked after rising from the soil.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p158#2/r6.claim: The point is that their lives were brief but disbelief led them to long punishment; ʿadad is a specification after kam, and al-Aʿmash reads it with tanwin.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p494#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p494#2/r1.speaker: نافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p494#2/r1.claim: They read قال كم لبثتم, making it God's question to the unbelievers; one view places the question on Resurrection Day, another after they enter Hell.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p494#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p494#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p494#2/r2.claim: They read قل كم لبثتم; it may address each person as O unbeliever, or command one person to speak to the group.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p494#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p494#2/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p494#2/r3.claim: They assimilate the thāʾ of لبثتم into tāʾ because the articulation points are close; others keep them distinct because the points differ.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p494#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p494#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p494#2/r4.claim: الأرض here may mean the graves or the world.

RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r1.claim: Kufan codices read “he said,” referring either to God or the angel ordered to question them; the other regional codices read “say,” referring to an angel or a leader of Hell's inhabitants.

RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r2.claim: The question is a rebuke: they denied any afterlife and imagined death as lasting extinction, so learning that Hell is eternal makes worldly life look brief and exposes their error.

RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r6.claim: Some say the question concerns their lifespan in this world: God gave them time to know and act, but they answer that it was short despite having been told the world is brief.

RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r7.claim: Others say it concerns their stay after death; they argue that “in the earth” points to the grave, though the wording can also describe activity in the world.

RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p110/r8.claim: The after-death view also appeals to criminals swearing they stayed no more than an hour, while believers say they remained until resurrection.

RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r1.speaker: منكرو عذاب القبر
RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r1.claim: Those denying grave punishment argue that if the dead were punished in their graves they would know their long stay and would not answer “a day or part of a day.”

RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r2.claim: The question may concern death with no life afterward until resurrection, a period that would include grave punishment.

RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p111/r3.claim: Alternatively, it asks how long they were together, excluding some people's earlier deaths, so their perceived answer can still be a day or part of one.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r1.claim: The question may ask how long they remained in their graves or how long they lived on earth; it is posed to disbelievers in the courts of Resurrection or in Hell.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r2.claim: The word for years is read with fatḥa on the nūn as a sound masculine plural, though some Arabs inflect it with kasra and tanwīn.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r6.claim: They read qul kam, an imperative: it may command the audience to say the answer, direct an angel to ask, or tell the Prophet to ask the disbeliever.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:112-114/r7.claim: Other readers use qal as a report that God or the angels asked them how long they remained.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:112/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:112/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:112/r1.claim: The questioner may be God or an appointed angel; it asks how long they lived on earth, either alive or in the graves, and years is a specification of how long.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:112/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:112/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وحمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:112/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read the question as an imperative addressed to the angel or one of Hell's leaders.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p132#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p132#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p132#4/r1.claim: The speaker may be God or an angel ordered to ask; the imperative reading “say” is attributed to Meccan, Ḥamza, and ʿAlī readers and orders Mālik to question them.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p132#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p132#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p132#4/r2.claim: “In the earth” refers to worldly life; “number of years” specifies the duration and is governed by “how long.”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p587/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p587/r8.speaker: حمزة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p587/r8.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn Kathīr read “qul kam” as an imperative addressed to an angel or another inhabitant of Hell; the remaining readers have “qāla,” spoken by God or an assigned angel.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p587/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p587/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p587/r9.claim: The question about years is a demand that fixes them to an answer; most read “ʿadada sinīn” as a construct, with “how many” measuring time and “number” specifying it. A reading with indefinite “ʿadadan” allows other parses, but “labithtum” as “you counted” is remote.

SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r1.speaker: الأخوان
SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r1.claim: The two readers use the imperative قل in both instances; Ibn Kathir matches them only in the first, while the remaining readers use قال as a report by God or an angel.

SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r2.claim: The two verbs lack alif in Kufan codices and include it in other regional codices; Hamza and Kisai follow Kufa, Asim differs or assumes a written omission, Ibn Kathir follows Mecca only in the second, and the others follow their codices.

SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r3.claim: كم is an accusative time adverb meaning how many years; عدد may be بدل of كم, as Abu al-Baqa says, but the author prefers عدد سنين as its specification.

SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r4.speaker: الأعمش والمفضل عن عاصم
SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r4.claim: They read عددا with tanwin; al-Lawamiʿ takes it as an advanced verbal-noun modifier, though the author says the Basran parse should be a circumstantial accusative.

SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r5.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r5.claim: A second analysis treats لبثتم as meaning counted, making عددا a verbal noun and سنين a بدل; al-Lawamiʿ calls this unlikely because staying does not imply counting.

SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:112/r6.claim: A third analysis makes عددا the specification of كم and سنين its بدل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p500/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p500/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p500/r1.claim: The question exposes how little of their short worldly lives they spent worshipping God; patience in that brief life would have brought the pious believers' success.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p500/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p500/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p500/r2.claim: They say they stayed a day or part of a day and are told to ask those who count the time.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p500/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p500/r4.speaker: أيفع بن عبد الكلاعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p500/r4.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says that, after the two groups enter their abodes, the people of Paradise call one brief day a good bargain for mercy and bliss, while the people of Hell made a bad bargain for fire and wrath.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p225#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p225#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p225#2/r1.claim: God asks how many years the unbelievers spent in the worldly life they considered victory; the wording recalls constricted years and exposes their delusion about worldly success.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p225#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p225#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p225#2/r2.claim: On the reading of the majority, God directly asks the question; Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read qul, making an appointed angel the speaker as God turns away from and punishes them.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p225#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p225#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p225#2/r3.claim: They are asked about worldly years in which they thought themselves victorious and dominant over their enemies.

DURR-FULL:v6p120/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p120/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p120/r8.claim: A report says God asks the people of Paradise how long they remained on earth.

BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p78#2/r1.claim: The earth is the world they ask to return to; لبث means staying continuously in a place, and عدد سنين specifies the number of years.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r1.claim: The questioner is God or the tasked angel, not a Hell leader; the question recalls worldly life they wanted back and rebukes denial of the Hereafter.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وابن كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r2.claim: These reciters read qul as an imperative to the angel, not a leader or all condemned represented by one.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r3.claim: ‘How many years did you remain on earth?’ asks how long they lived in the world they seek to return to.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r4.claim: ʿAdadan specifies kam and is temporal adverb for ‘remained’; Abū al-Baqāʾ instead parses it as apposition to kam.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r5.speaker: الأعمش والمفضل عن عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v18p69#3/r5.claim: They read ʿadadan with nunation; al-Rāzī takes sinīn as temporal adverb and ʿadadan as a verbal noun used as a noun before its modifier, while Abū al-Baqāʾ makes sinīn appositional.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r6.claim: The most likely answer to when the trumpet is blown is the later question about how long they stayed on earth; intervening material is parenthetical.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p130#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p130#2/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p130#2/r1.claim: The majority read qāla in the past tense, placing the question after the trumpet and resurrection; it is most likely the answer to the earlier conditional in 23:101.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p130#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p130#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p130#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects placing the question after unbelievers enter Hell as inconsistent with the discourse; the intervening verses are digressions.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p130#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p130#2/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p130#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read qul as an imperative addressed to the angel tasked with reviving the dead.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p131/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p131/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p131/r2.claim: The question about years alerts them to their error: they had claimed that those buried in earth would never emerge.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p131/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p131/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p131/r3.claim: Adad sinīn is a specification of the interrogative kam; sinīn is the actual specification, and adad reinforces the quantity already asked about.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p131/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p131/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p131/r5.claim: The question and answer indirectly prove they emerged alive from earth, refuting their denial and their claim that life cannot return to bones and remains after centuries.

TABATABAI:23:99-118#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:99-118#4/r1.claim: The question about years spent on earth concerns the time in graves, not simply worldly life; a proposal to include both worldly life and barzakh is also mentioned.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p237/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p237/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p237/r9.claim: Rejecters think worldly life is long and deny accountability or return to God, but the Hereafter will make its brevity clear and expose the inability of their deities and intercessors to help.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p279/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p279/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p279/r1.claim: Rejecters will discover that the respite they thought long passed in a blink; they will then deeply regret their conduct.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r6.claim: The delay in resurrection will soon be exposed as a misconception: what people imagined to be a long earthly life will end like a blink.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r7.claim: The opening question's qala is not spoken by God or an angel; it means that some speaker will ask.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p284/r8.claim: The words qala are understood in the sense qala qail, meaning that a speaker will speak.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r1.claim: The dialogue about earthly life occurs among the people themselves, as the parallel exchange in Ṭāhā makes explicit.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p285/r3.claim: People assume they will keep living only while alive; after life passes, it becomes a dream of the past.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:112/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:112/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:112/r1.claim: The afterlife dialogue is representative: earthly time is a perception shaped by worldly conditions, and passage into eternal life changes one’s sense of time.

QIRAAT-ER:23:112:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:112:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:23:112:1#1/r1.claim: The imperative changes a narrative report into a direct command to the Prophet.

STUDYQURAN:23:112/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:112/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:112/r1.claim: The Hereafter makes people view their whole worldly life as no more than a day or hour.

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.claim: The conclusion warns that disbelievers facing their perdition will wish to return to do good instead of evil, but it will be too late.
